questions.question: If stopping takes longer than normal, you should:

options.text: Follow closer than usual.
Follow farther away than usual.
Ride on the shoulder.
Let someone else ride your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow farther away than usual.
questions.explanation: Leave more space behind the vehicle ahead if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Keep at least a three-second distance if the road is slippery, if you cannot see past the vehicle in front, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: Do not change gears on railroad tracks because:

options.text: Your motorcycle may stall.
You might go too fast.
Other drivers may not expect it.
The uneven surface makes shifting harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may stall.
questions.explanation: Do not shift gears while crossing railroad tracks. Your motorcycle might stall while on the tracks.

questions.question: If the throttle is stuck, you should:

options.text: Jump off the motorcycle.
Use the brakes.
Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Leave the throttle alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: If the throttle sticks, try twisting it back and forth several times. If this does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch right away.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Use your high beam.
Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Be visible.
Ride only on the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only on the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: At night, use your high beam (unless you are following or meeting another car), use other vehicles' headlights to help you see, and wear reflective clothing. Choose your lane position based on what helps you see, be seen, and maintain safe distance.

questions.question: When stopping, it is best to:

options.text: Grab the front brake lever hard.
Keep your knees on the gas tank and look ahead.
Put more and more pressure on the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees on the gas tank and look ahead.
questions.explanation: Apply the brakes smoothly and firmly. As weight moves forward, the front wheel gets more grip, so you can use more front brake force and less rear brake force. Keep your knees on the gas tank and look ahead to stay in a straight line.

questions.question: During acceleration, a sidecar will:

options.text: Feel like it is falling behind.
Feel like it is accelerating faster than the motorcycle.
Shake uncontrollably.
Make acceleration feel faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel like it is falling behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is an unpowered weight attached to your motorcycle. Because of its inertia, it feels like it lags behind when you speed up.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handle grip toward the direction you want to go.
Press the handle grip away from the direction you want to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip toward the direction you want to go.
questions.explanation: To swerve and avoid a hazard, press the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press right to straighten up. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle best, a rider should:

options.text: Sit with arms fully stretched out.
Use their arms to hold their body up.
Keep their knees away from the gas tank.
Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not hold you up. Your arms should be slightly bent. Keep your knees on the gas tank and your feet firmly on the footrests to help balance.

questions.question: If it starts to rain while you are riding, you should:

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Speed up.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Stop on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil buildup and is unsafe when wet. When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by other cars. Slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: When entering a highway or curve, group riders should:

options.text: Ride single-file.
Ride in a staggered formation.
Ride in pairs.
Ride on the far right of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride single-file.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation works well normally, but switch to single-file when turning, going through curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When turning left, what should you do?

options.text: Press the right handgrip.
Press the left handgrip.
Press both handgrips at the same time.
Do not press either handgrip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the left handgrip.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn to make the motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: To carry a passenger, which of the following do you NOT need to adjust?

options.text: Tire pressure.
Mirror positions.
Headlight position.
Brake light position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake light position.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle sits differently with a passenger due to extra weight. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, shocks, headlight, and mirrors. You do not need to adjust the brake light position.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up before hitting it.
Slow down before hitting it.
Lean the motorcycle.
Stay seated on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before hitting it.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid hitting an obstacle, slow down as much as you can first. Try to hit it at a 90-degree angle. Keep the motorcycle upright, rise slightly off the seat, and roll back the throttle just before impact.

questions.question: Which statement is true about motorcycle brakes?

options.text: The front and rear brakes provide equal stopping power.
The front brake provides more stopping power than the rear brake.
The rear brake provides more stopping power than the front brake.
Use only the front brake when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake provides more stopping power than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the total stopping power. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: As your weight moves forward while braking, what happens?

options.text: You can apply the front brake harder.
You should use less pressure on the front brake.
You can apply the rear brake harder.
You lose traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can apply the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: When your weight shifts forward during braking, the front wheel gets more traction. This means you can apply more pressure to the front brake.

questions.question: What should motorcycle riders do about hearing protection?

options.text: Wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
Wear hearing protection only on long rides.
Do not wear hearing protection because it will block important sounds like horns and sirens.
Do not wear hearing protection if you are wearing a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing damage over time, even with a full-face helmet. Ear plugs and other hearing protection can prevent damage while still letting you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: When going through a curve, what should you remember?

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane through the entire curve.
Always stay in the left part of the lane through the entire curve.
Always stay in the right part of the lane through the entire curve.
The best path may not follow the curve of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The best path may not follow the curve of the road.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly. Be ready to change your lane position as needed. The best path through a curve does not always match the shape of the road.

questions.question: Is it a good idea to ride on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, because the driver will see you easily.
No, because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
Yes, because a passenger may tell the driver you are there.
No, because it is illegal. You must ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane where the driver is most likely to see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, how should you look?

options.text: Turn just your head.
Turn your head and shoulders.
Turn just your shoulders.
Turn your entire body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When riding with a heavy load, what should you adjust?

options.text: Brakes.
Seat.
Suspension.
Brake light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Suspension.
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to match the manufacturer's recommendations for that weight.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When traffic is light.
When traffic is heavy.
When you can see the road through vehicles in front of you.
When the weather is pleasant and clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic is heavy.
questions.explanation: A two-second following distance works in normal conditions. But increase your distance when you need more room to stop. This includes bad weather, nighttime, when you cannot see ahead, and heavy traffic.

questions.question: A rectangular sign can be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Signs that show road rules, like speed limits, are rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: How do you stop another vehicle from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Swerve from side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane. This discourages car drivers from trying to share your space.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: The middle of the lane has an oily buildup. You should:

options.text: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
Ride only on the oily strip for better grip.
Avoid the entire center of the lane.
Not worry about oil or other items in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars builds up in the center of lanes. On dry roads, this strip usually still has enough grip for a motorcycle. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride around it and still be in the center portion of your lane. Avoid it when the road is wet.
